To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present an algorithm for tuning graded thresholds in real-time traffic light controllers and show that the proposed tuning algorithm improves performance of the controllers significantly.

we propose a stochastic threshold-tuning algorithm that can be combined with any graded-threshold-based traffic light control algorithm and that we show through simulation that this combination results in improved performance.

we propose a novel threshold-tuning algorithm that can be combined with any threshold-based TLC algorithm, and we show the effectiveness of our tuning algorithm by combining it with three novel TLC algorithms and by demonstrating the improvement in their performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a new algorithm for tuning the thresholds that are used by TLC algorithms and three novel graded-threshold-based algorithms for TLC, and the results show a significant improvement in the performance of the TLC algorithms.
the design of a threshold-tuning algorithm and its integration with several TLC algorithms to obtain a better performance.
a novel approach to tune the thresholds associated with a TLC scheme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed threshold-tuning algorithm provides an effective means of improving the performance of any graded-threshold-based traffic light control algorithm, and it can also be used to obtain an “optimized” representation of the state space in the case of full-state Q-learning algorithms.
our threshold-tuning scheme, when used in conjunction with any TLC algorithm, is an optimal way to tune the thresholds for the TLC algorithm.
our threshold-tuning scheme can improve the performance of any threshold-based traffic-light control algorithm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the threshold-tuning scheme can be used to improve the performance of a TLC algorithm without any significant additional computational cost.

we have presented a novel threshold-tuning scheme for graded-threshold-based traffic-light control, which, when integrated in a graded-threshold-based control algorithm, can significantly improve the performance of the algorithm.

we present an incremental-update online tuning scheme for graded thresholds that is integrated with three novel TLC algorithms, namely, 1) a state-aggregated Q-learning, 2) Q-learning with function approximation, and 3 ) a priority-based TLC algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tuning of thresholds can be done online and is not an offline process.
the tuning algorithm can be integrated with any TLC algorithm based on graded thresholds.
the tuning of thresholds can be used to enhance the performance of TLC algorithms that are based on graded signal control.
